source_title: Yorùbá Òrìṣà Traditions — Ọ̀rúnmìlà-focused Ifá witness
continuity: Bounded UNESCO/Smithsonian Ifá witness; living Yorùbá sacred-tradition context
work_or_witness: UNESCO Ifa divination system (2008); Smithsonian Divination cup label (accession 92-10-1)
description: The individually named Ifá figure in the selected witnesses. UNESCO calls Ifa or Orunmila a mystical figure regarded by the Yoruba as associated with wisdom and intellectual development; the Smithsonian label describes diviner-priests consulting Orunmila for guidance in its object-specific Ifá context.

being_types.note: A source-native sacred-context description. It is not mapped to a generic fantasy race, class, moral alignment, or an exhaustive pantheon category.

cultures.note: UNESCO's community context. It does not collapse diverse Yorùbá communities, regional lineages, or diaspora traditions into one homogeneous culture.

metaphysical_laws_and_rituals.note: The witnesses place Ọ̀rúnmìlà in a living divinatory system; this does not disclose restricted knowledge or reconstruct ritual procedure.

canon_status: individually named sacred figure in the selected bounded institutional witnesses

supports: Ifa or Orunmila as a mystical figure and association with wisdom/intellectual development
babaláwo consult Orunmila for guidance in the documented Ifá object context

comparison_cautions: Ọ̀rúnmìlà is a living sacred-tradition figure, not a fictional game character. The English institutional word 'deity' is not treated as an exact, universal translation or a license to flatten Òrìṣà into 'gods.'
No moral alignment, combat power, class, race, kinship, personality, origin story, or relationship is inferred.
This Yoruba-focused witness is not merged with Afro-Brazilian, Caribbean, Cuban, or other diaspora traditions, even where names or practices may be related.
